headline: NerdWallet: priced for disruption, but still growing and buying back stock
subheadline: At ~3x EBITDA the market assumes the auto-insurance gap and AI search break the model. Our bear case is still above the share price
narrative: NerdWallet runs comparison and guidance content for credit cards, loans, insurance, banking and small-business finance. It earns referral fees when users take out products.

Q3 2026 revenue grew 11% to $239.6m, with strong lending and deposits. But auto-insurance revenue fell $17.4m on lower lead volumes, and full-year profit guidance was cut for the second quarter running.
The shares have fallen to about half their 52-week high. At $7.46 the company trades at about 3x EBITDA and under 9x earnings, with net cash.
Management bought back $99m of stock in the first nine months of 2026, roughly a fifth of today's market value.
We weight a recovery case and an AI-disruption case 50/50, which gives a $13 target. The rating is Buy, but with high uncertainty.
market_pricing: EV of about $390m against LTM EBITDA of $114m and free cash flow of $131m.
Q4 2026 revenue guidance implies a 13% decline year on year, and management flagged Q1 2027 as the toughest comparison.
Analysts are cautious: 1 Buy, 3 Hold and 1 Sell, with a median target of $8.50.

business.title: A personal-finance marketplace funded by referral fees
business.subtitle: Consumers and small businesses compare financial products; providers pay per lead or per approval
overview: Based in San Francisco, with about 650 employees. Co-founder Tim Chen is CEO.
Revenue is reported for two user groups from 2026: Consumer ($214.5m in Q3, up 12%) and SMB ($25.1m, up 6%).
In Q3, the main drivers were student loans (+$25.0m), personal loans (+$13.3m) and deposits (+$8.6m), offset by auto insurance (–$17.4m).

segments.name: Consumer
segments.text: Credit cards, loans, banking, insurance and investing referrals. 90% of Q3 2026 revenue.

segments.name: SMB
segments.text: Small-business loans and financial products. 10% of Q3 2026 revenue.

business.financials_title: Profitable since 2025, but margins are back under pressure
financial_points: Revenue grew from $539m (2022) to $837m (2025), and the EBIT margin turned from –3% to +8%.
Free cash flow was $113m in 2025. 2026 guidance: adjusted EBITDA $127–133m and GAAP operating income $56–62m.
Cash fell to $73.5m at September 2026 (from $98.3m) after $99m of buybacks.

industry.title: Online financial-product marketing is cyclical and changing with AI search
industry.subtitle: Volumes follow credit conditions and insurer ad budgets; traffic sources are shifting
market: Comparison sites earn more when lenders want growth and insurers want new policies. Both swing with credit and claims cycles.
Auto insurers raised marketing spend in 2025–26, but NerdWallet cannot yet monetise several top-10 carriers.
Search is changing: AI answers reduce clicks through to publishers, which threatens organic traffic.

tailwinds.title: Lending recovery
tailwinds.text: Personal loans, student loans and deposits are all growing strongly in 2026.

tailwinds.title: Direct relationships
tailwinds.text: Investment in app users and logged-in members reduces reliance on search.

headwinds.title: Auto-insurance gap
headwinds.text: Carrier and agent partnerships are taking longer than expected. Management said its timelines were 'overly optimistic'.

headwinds.title: Paid-marketing cost
headwinds.text: Q3 sales & marketing rose 28% to $173m, which halved the operating margin to 8%.

industry.source: NerdWallet Q3 2026 release and call (5 Nov 2026); Earnings Whispers (5 Nov 2026)

competition.title: A scaled brand in a field of performance marketers
competition.subtitle: Trades below lead-gen peers on every multiple
points: Peers such as LendingTree, MediaAlpha, EverQuote and QuinStreet monetise similar traffic. EverQuote and MediaAlpha are more exposed to auto insurance.
NerdWallet's brand and editorial reach are its edge, but they depend on search and AI distribution.
porter: Intense: comparison sites, bank and insurer direct channels, Credit Karma.
AI assistants answering 'best credit card' questions directly.
Low technical barriers; the barrier is brand trust and partner integrations.
Traffic sources (Google, app stores) hold much of the power.
Financial providers move budgets quickly between channels based on cost per acquisition.
competition.source: NerdWallet filings; peer data from Yahoo Finance

theses.title: 1. The valuation already prices in a lot of damage
theses.subtitle: Even our AI-disruption scenario is worth more than the share price
points: EV is about 3.4x LTM EBITDA and 3x LTM free cash flow, against a peer median EV/EBITDA of about 9x.
Our bear case assumes flat revenue in 2027, then a 1–2% decline a year with margins stuck at 6%. It still gives $9.65 a share.
Net cash and positive cash flow mean the company does not need outside capital to get through the auto-insurance gap.
theses.risk: Revenue keeps falling well beyond Q4 2026's 13% decline, or margins go negative again as marketing costs rise.
theses.source: Yahoo Finance via research pack; analyst scenarios

theses.title: 2. Buybacks are shrinking the share count fast
theses.subtitle: $99m repurchased in nine months, about a fifth of the current market value
points: Buybacks in the first nine months of 2026 were $99.3m, five times the prior-year period ($19.5m).
At today's price, continued buybacks at that pace would retire a large share of the company each year.
Cash fell to $73.5m, so future buybacks need to come from operating cash flow, which is still positive.
theses.risk: Cash flow falls far enough that buybacks stop, or the company does a large acquisition instead.

theses.title: 3. The growth engines outside auto insurance are working
theses.subtitle: Revenue grew 11% in Q3 despite a $17m auto-insurance hole
points: Lending and banking more than offset auto insurance in Q3: student loans +$25.0m, personal loans +$13.3m, deposits +$8.6m.
Q3 revenue beat consensus. The miss was on profit, because marketing spend rose faster than revenue.
If auto-insurance partnerships are rebuilt in 2027, operating leverage could return quickly. This is our recovery case ($16.55).
theses.risk: Lending demand weakens with the credit cycle at the same time as the auto-insurance gap persists.

comps.title: NerdWallet trades at a deep discount to online lead-generation peers
comps.subtitle: About 3x EBITDA vs a peer median of about 9x
comps.note: Peers: online performance-marketing and comparison marketplaces.

dcf.subtitle: Recovery case: consensus growth to 2027, fading to 2.5%; operating margin recovers from 6.5% toward 10%

valuation.title: A wide range of outcomes, most of them above the share price
points: Our $13 target is well above the analyst median ($8.50), because we treat buybacks and net cash as a floor.
The probability between recovery and disruption is the key judgement. We assume 50/50.

risks.title: AI search is the existential risk; auto insurance is the near-term one

items.risk: AI answers reduce organic traffic and referral volume
items.mitigant: Investment in app users and logged-in members, and AI products of its own. Our bear case models the decline.

items.risk: Auto-insurance partnerships take longer than expected
items.mitigant: Other verticals grew enough to lift Q3 revenue 11% anyway.

items.risk: Marketing costs keep rising faster than revenue
items.mitigant: Spend can be cut quickly. Management has shown it can run the business for profit (2025 EBIT margin 8%).

catalysts.what: The toughest year-on-year comparison, per management.
Share buybacks from operating cash flow.

risks.source: NerdWallet Q3 2026 release and call; Yahoo Finance earnings calendar
